questions.text: You are organizing your school's annual Diwali Mela. What is your main job in the committee?

options.A: Going shop to shop in the local market, chatting up uncles to give sponsorship money for the event.
options.B: Sitting with the budget diary, calculating exactly how much we need for lights vs. DJ so the school doesn't go broke.
options.C: Designing the sponsor brochure on Canva, making the mela look like the biggest party of the year.
options.D: Sitting with the Principal and the head sponsor to finalize the big deal and sign the permissions.

questions.text: Your older sibling wants to sell their 5-year-old Activa to buy a new bike. How do you help?

options.A: Calling up your friends and neighbours to find a buyer and hyping up how good the mileage still is.
options.B: Checking OLX, comparing prices of similar Activas, accounting for scratches, to calculate the exact perfect selling price.
options.C: Taking aesthetic photos of the scooter, washing it, and writing a killer WhatsApp forward to send around.
options.D: Stepping in when the buyer actually comes to your house, doing the hard bargaining, and walking away with extra cash.

questions.text: It's your best friend's birthday and you want to throw them a surprise party at a nice cafe. What's your move?

options.A: Personally calling everyone, convincing them to come, and making sure the hype is real.
options.B: Making a Splitwise group, calculating exactly who owes how much per head, including GST and service charge.
options.C: Creating a secret WhatsApp group with a cool digital invite and a mood board for the dress code.
options.D: Taking charge at the cafe, negotiating a discount with the manager for bringing a large group of 15 kids.

questions.text: When you sit with your family to watch Shark Tank India, what do you focus on the most?

options.A: The founder's energy—how they talk, how they pitch, and how they handle the Sharks' cross-questioning.
options.B: The unit economics—when Aman Gupta or Namita Thapar ask about EBITDA, gross margins, and customer acquisition cost.
options.C: The product packaging, the branding, and how beautiful their presentation slides look on screen.
options.D: The final negotiation—who offers what equity, the counter-offers, and who walks away with the best deal.

questions.text: The teacher assigns a massive History group project. What is your role in the team?

options.A: Convincing the teacher to give your group the coolest topic and keeping team morale high so everyone actually works.
options.B: Doing the deep research, finding exact dates and facts, and compiling all the raw data into a massive Word doc.
options.C: Taking all the boring text and turning it into a beautiful, color-coordinated chart paper or PPT.
options.D: Assigning tasks to everyone, making sure deadlines are met, and doing the final presentation in front of the class.

questions.text: You and your cousins are planning a Goa trip for after your 10th boards. What are you doing?

options.A: Talking to your strict parents and uncles, pitching them why this trip is safe and a great idea.
options.B: Creating a master Excel sheet with flight costs, hotel prices per night, and an exact daily food budget.
options.C: Making a reel-style itinerary showing all the cool shacks, beaches, and cafes you guys will visit to get everyone excited.
options.D: Making the final decision on the hotel, booking everything, and solving arguments when two cousins want different things.

questions.text: It's time for the Head Boy/Head Girl elections. If you were involved, you'd most likely be:

options.A: The campaign manager, shaking hands in the corridors and getting the popular kids to vote for your candidate.
options.B: Looking at the voting demographics—calculating how many votes from Section A and B are needed to guarantee a win.
options.C: Making the posters, writing the catchy slogans, and directing the campaign video.
options.D: The candidate themselves, giving the final powerful speech on stage and uniting the whole school.

questions.text: The IPL Mega Auction is live on TV. What fascinates you the most about the event?

options.A: The scouts who built relationships with young, unknown players long before they became famous.
options.B: The stats—how the analysts calculate a player's strike rate vs price tag to see if they are a 'value buy'.
options.C: The team jersey reveals, the hype videos, and how the franchise builds its brand on Instagram after a buy.
options.D: The team owner lifting the paddle, outsmarting other teams, and securing the star player at the buzzer.

questions.text: Two of your best friends had a huge fight. How do you fix the situation?

options.A: Meeting them both separately for momos, listening to them, and slowly getting them back on talking terms.
options.B: Mentally listing out who started it, who is actually at fault logically, and what exactly needs to be apologized for.
options.C: Making a funny meme or a group video call to break the ice and make them laugh so they forget the tension.
options.D: Making them sit face-to-face, laying down the facts, and telling them to shake hands and end this drama right now.

questions.text: Honestly, what sounds like the coolest way to be successful when you grow up?

options.A: Having a massive network of powerful people on your speed dial and flying around the world to meet them.
options.B: Being the smartest person in the room who can look at complex numbers and predict exactly what will happen.
options.C: Making things look so incredibly good that people can't help but buy into your vision.
options.D: Being the boss who sits at the head of the table, signs the multi-crore deals, and leads the empire.

Deal Broker / Relationship Manager.title: The Networker (Deal Broker / Relationship Manager)
Deal Broker / Relationship Manager.primary_match_text: You are a people person! You know how to talk, how to convince, and how to build trust. In Investment Banking, you'd be the one flying across the world, meeting CEOs, and bringing in the massive deals.
Deal Broker / Relationship Manager.day_in_the_life: Your day starts with breakfast with a tech startup founder, followed by calls with massive investors. You spend your time pitching ideas, smoothing out relationships, and making sure clients trust your bank with their money.
Deal Broker / Relationship Manager.alternative_match_text: If not in Investment Banking, you'd make an amazing PR Executive, Corporate Sales Head, or a Startup Founder.
Deal Broker / Relationship Manager.educational_roadmap: Take Commerce in 11th/12th. Pursue a BBA or B.Com (Hons) from top colleges like NMIMS, Christ, or DU. Focus heavily on debate and networking. The ultimate goal is an MBA from a top IIM or ISB to build a powerful alumni network.

Financial Modeler / Equity Researcher.title: The Brain (Financial Modeler / Equity Researcher)
Financial Modeler / Equity Researcher.primary_match_text: You are a logical genius who loves numbers. You don't just guess; you calculate. In Investment Banking, you'd be the wizard who looks at an Excel sheet and tells a company exactly how much they are worth down to the last rupee.
Financial Modeler / Equity Researcher.day_in_the_life: You sit with three monitors, analyzing market trends, company balance sheets, and building complex Excel models. When the big bosses need to know if buying a company makes mathematical sense, they turn to you.
Financial Modeler / Equity Researcher.alternative_match_text: If not in Investment Banking, you'd be a brilliant Data Scientist, Actuary, or Hedge Fund Manager.
Financial Modeler / Equity Researcher.educational_roadmap: Take Commerce with Math or PCM in 11th/12th. Pursue B.Com (Hons), Eco (Hons) from SRCC/St. Stephens, or even B.Tech from an IIT. Clearing the CA (Chartered Accountant) or CFA (Chartered Financial Analyst) exams will make you unstoppable.

Pitchbook Designer / Syndication Expert.title: The Storyteller (Pitchbook Designer / Syndication Expert)
Pitchbook Designer / Syndication Expert.primary_match_text: You have an eye for design and a talent for making things look convincing. In Investment Banking, numbers mean nothing if they aren't presented well. You create the 'Pitchbooks'—the beautiful, high-stakes presentations that win multi-crore deals.
Pitchbook Designer / Syndication Expert.day_in_the_life: You take the complex math from the analysts and turn it into visual masterpieces. You design the slides, structure the story of the deal, and make sure the presentation is so sharp that the client can't say no.
Pitchbook Designer / Syndication Expert.alternative_match_text: If not in Investment Banking, you'd thrive as a UI/UX Designer, Brand Strategist, or Creative Director.
Pitchbook Designer / Syndication Expert.educational_roadmap: Take any stream in 11th/12th (Commerce preferred). Pursue a BBA, B.Com, or a degree in Design/Mass Comm with a strong understanding of finance. An MBA in Marketing or Finance will help you bridge the gap between creativity and business.

M&A Managing Director.title: The Boss (M&A Managing Director)
M&A Managing Director.primary_match_text: You are a natural leader who loves taking charge and making the final call. In Investment Banking, you'd be the Managing Director—the one who oversees the whole merger, negotiates the final price, and closes the massive deals.
M&A Managing Director.day_in_the_life: You are the captain of the ship. You guide the analysts, direct the presentation, and sit at the head of the boardroom table. When it's time to negotiate the final hundreds of crores, you do the talking.
M&A Managing Director.alternative_match_text: If not in Investment Banking, you'd be a CEO, a Venture Capitalist, or a successful Entrepreneur.
M&A Managing Director.educational_roadmap: Take Commerce with Math or PCM in 11th/12th. Get into a premium undergrad college (IIT, SRCC, Shaheed Sukhdev). Crack the CAT exam to get into IIM Ahmedabad, Bangalore, or Calcutta. It takes years of grinding as an analyst to get promoted to this boss level!
